helpIntro: Carnegie Mellon undergraduates use a 4.0 Quality Point Average (QPA) scale. Enter factorable CMU units and final grades; A=4, B=3, C=2, D=1, R=0.
helpNote: For undergraduate records. P/N/O/W/I/AD are non-factorable. Graduate students use a different 4.33 scale. Repeat Impact is unavailable because every graded attempt remains in QPA.
helpExample: A 12-unit A earns 48 quality points and a 9-unit B earns 27. Together, 75 ÷ 21 = 3.571.

gradeExplanations.R: R is failure: zero quality points; factorable units remain in QPA.
gradeExplanations.N: Not passing pass/no pass grade; non-factorable.
gradeExplanations.I: Incomplete; non-factorable until replaced by a permanent grade.
gradeExplanations.AD: Transfer or examination credit notation; non-factorable.

specialTypes.name: Carnegie Mellon course
specialTypes.note: Use the final undergraduate transcript grade and CMU units.

specialTypes.name: External transfer or exam credit
specialTypes.note: Ordinary external transfer/exam credit does not enter CMU QPA.

specialTypes.name: University cross-registration course
specialTypes.note: CMU cross-registration program courses have grades recorded and are factored into QPA; use the CMU transcript grade and units.

specialTypes.name: Graduate-level course taken as undergraduate
specialTypes.note: Any +/- final grade is converted to the corresponding undergraduate letter grade before QPA calculation.

repeatPolicy.note: Enter every graded attempt as a separate completed course. Repeat Impact is disabled because CMU does not replace the earlier QPA grade.
